questions.definition: A death of a patient, user or other person that the information reasonably suggests.

Serious injury (21 CFR 803.3(w)) is an injury or illness that is life-threatening, results in permanent impairment of a body function or permanent damage to a body structure, or needs medical or surgical intervention to preclude such permanent impairment or damage. Permanent means irreversible, excluding trivial impairment or damage. Answer each part on its own.
questions.explanation: Our procedure (sample QP-08): permanent means it does not heal by itself or with treatment. An injury that needed treatment to prevent permanent damage is part (c), even if the patient recovered.
questions.text: Serious injury, part (a): is the injury or illness life-threatening?

Permanent means irreversible, excluding trivial impairment or damage. Answer each part on its own.
questions.explanation: Our procedure (sample QP-08): permanent means it does not heal by itself or with treatment. An injury that needed treatment to prevent permanent damage is part (c), even if the patient recovered.
questions.text: Serious injury, part (b): does it result in permanent impairment of a body function or permanent damage to a body structure?

questions.definition: Serious injury (21 CFR 803.3(w)) is an injury or illness that is life-threatening, results in permanent impairment of a body function or permanent damage to a body structure, or needs medical or surgical intervention to preclude such permanent impairment or damage. Permanent means irreversible, excluding trivial impairment or damage. Answer each part on its own.
questions.examples: Sample examples: a cut closed with sutures to prevent permanent scarring is part (c); a bruise that healed without treatment is not.
questions.explanation: Our procedure (sample QP-08): permanent means it does not heal by itself or with treatment. An injury that needed treatment to prevent permanent damage is part (c), even if the patient recovered.
questions.text: Serious injury, part (c): does it need medical or surgical intervention to preclude permanent impairment of a body function or permanent damage to a body structure?

questions.definition: Caused or contributed (21 CFR 803.3(c)): the death or serious injury was, or may have been, attributed to the device, including through its failure, malfunction, improper or inadequate design, manufacture or labelling, or user error.
questions.text: Did the device cause or contribute to the death or serious injury?

questions.definition: Malfunction (21 CFR 803.3(k)): the device failed to meet its performance specifications or otherwise perform as intended.
A malfunction is reportable when the device, or a similar device you market, would be likely to cause or contribute to a death or serious injury if the malfunction were to recur.
questions.note: Recurrence is presumed: answer what would follow if it recurred, not whether it will recur. A No needs its reason.
questions.text: Would the malfunction be likely to cause or contribute to a death or serious injury if it were to recur?

questions.definition: Remedial action (21 CFR 803.3(v)) is any action other than routine maintenance or servicing of a device where such action is necessary to prevent recurrence of a reportable event. Yes gives the 5-work-day report (803.53); otherwise a reportable event gets the 30-calendar-day report (803.50).
questions.text: Is remedial action needed to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to the public health, or has FDA asked in writing for a 5-day report?

questions.definition: Under VMSR, eligible malfunction reports may be sent quarterly in summary form. Record the answer and the product code: the reporting route is chosen when the report is prepared. This answer never changes the conclusion.
questions.note: Sample: check the product code against FDA's VMSR list.
questions.text: Does our organization take part in FDA's Voluntary Malfunction Summary Reporting (VMSR) program for this device's product code?
